headline: Approved Order of Conditions for 234 Calvary Street and a wetlands determination for the 231 Second Ave parking lot.
summary: The commission authorized its Chair or Conservation Agent to sign off on the 1000 Winter Street development prospectus. It approved a wetlands determination for the parking lot at 231 Second Ave and an Order of Conditions for 234 Calvary Street. It also agreed to allow a tree removal at 137 Copeland Street.
decisions: Authorized the Chair or Conservation Agent to sign off on the 1000 Winter Street development prospectus, 5-0 with one abstention.
Issued a Positive 2B/Negative 3 determination for 231 Second Ave, with a condition to record the O&M plan at the Registry of Deeds, 6-0.
Issued an Order of Conditions for 234 Calvary Street, including standard special conditions, 6-0.
Agreed that the tree removal at 137 Copeland Street should be allowed.
Approved the minutes of the 9-24-2026 meeting, 4-0 with two abstentions.

decision_titles: Development prospectus sign-off for 1000 Winter Street
Wetlands determination for parking lot at 231 Second Ave
Notice of Intent (DEP File # 316-0855) for 234 Calvary Street
plain_text:
Approved 10/22/2026 
  
 
Waltham Conservation Commission 
October 8, 2026 
Meeting Minutes 
Meeting took place via public Zoom call with participation information posted at City Hall, Government 
Center, and on the Commission’s page of the city web site. Zoom information was circulated directly 
to all applicants and others on the public agenda. 
Meeting called to order at 7:02 PM. 
Attendees: Chair Bill Doyle, Vice Chair Lisa Limonciello, Gerard Dufromont, Michael Donovan, Anja 
Shafer, Frank Fitzgerald. Conservation Agent Julia Abbott. 
Absent:  
Development Prospectus Sign Off 
• 1000 Winter Street. Chris Carr of BXP and Nick Skoly of VHB were present. Mr. Carr 
summarized the project. This is planned residential redevelopment in the recently created 
zoning overlay district. The specific site is a building within the Bay Colony office park. This will 
include demolition of an empty approximately 280,000 sq.ft. office building, to be replaced by a 
283-unit multi-family apartment building, using existing foundations as much as possible. He 
noted that they have been working with Cambridge Water Department to address any 
concerns [the site is in the Hobbs Brook Reservoir watershed]. There are no jurisdictional 
areas on the site. Ms. Limonciello asked a question regarding erosion control approvals. Mr. 
Skoly added that they will still need Engineering Department approval and they will meet all 
standards. He added that storm water on the site is not currently treated, but will be in the new 
design. BXP also has a pilot program to reduce or do away with winter salt use, and this 
property will use that. Mr. Dufromont, as an abutter, asked about communication with residents 
of the Lincoln Woods neighborhood. Mr. Carr stated they are just starting the process and 
hope to be in front of the city council in November, and they plan to hold neighbor meetings 
soon. Mr. Dufromont asked about start dates; Mr. Carr stated at the earliest it would be late 
summer or early fall 2027. Motion authorizing the Chair or Conservation Agent to sign off on 
behalf of the Commission made by Mr. Donovan, seconded by Mr. Dufromont. In favor: Doyle, 
Limonciello, Donovan, Shafer, Fitzgerald. Abstain: Mr. Dufromont. Motion passed. 
 
Public Meeting 
Request for Determination of Applicability (continued from 9-24-2026) 
Applicant: Devin McArthur 
Property Location: 231 Second Ave 
Project Description: Reclaim, grade, pave, and stripe 37,370 sq.ft. commercial parking lot. No 
change to the current parking lot dimensions, only reestablishing a solid gravel base and repaving. 
Mr. McArthur and Bob Quinn were present. Mr. McArthur presented a revised plan of the work area 
and noted that pavement has been reduced from the original proposal. The total work area will be 
37,700 sq.ft., but only 33,375 sq.ft. of pavement. They will return approximately 4,525 sq.ft. to green 
space. They will install 3 wetlands signs, 3 de-icing signs, and plant a total of 56 native shrubs, as
Approved 10/22/2026 
well as reseed those areas. Ms. Abbott added that she, the applicant, and Cambridge Water 
Department worked out this modified and improved plan and everyone is satisfied with it. She 
commented that Mr. McArthur did a very good job. He has also submitted an O&M plan, which based 
on a previous order of conditions had been inadequate. This also includes storm water 
improvements. She recommended that the commission issue a Positive 2B / Negative 3 
determination. She also recommended that the determination include a condition that the O&M plan 
be recorded at the Registry of Deeds. Ms. Limonciello noted no drainage and run-off details on the 
plan. Mr. McArthur confirmed there is presently no storm water infrastructure; water now drains, and 
will continue to drain, off the parking lot into the current and to-be expanded rain garden areas. It 
does not go to the street. Ms. Limonciello asked for clarification of the parcel location. Mr. Daly from 
the commission office shared a city GIS view locating the parcel. He noted no existing city storm 
water drainage, and that flow from here is to the west, into Weston below the Hobbs Brook basin and 
then toward the Stony Brook basin, which is why CWD is involved. Motion to issue a Positive 
2B/Negative 3 determination by Ms. Limonciello; seconded by Ms. Shafer. Motion amended by Ms. 
Limonciello to include a requirement to record the O&M at the Registry of Deeds; seconded by Ms. 
Shafer. In favor: Doyle, Limonciello, Donovan, Shafer, Fitzgerald, Dufromont. Motion passed. Mr. 
Doyle asked for scheduling details. Mr. Quinn stated they expect to do this in November. Mr. Doyle 
asked them to also keep CWD informed. 
 
Public Hearing 
Notice of Intent (DEP File # 316-0855) (Continued from 9-24-2026) 
Applicant: George Sarris 
Property Location: 234 Calvary Street 
Project Description: Raze an existing commercial building and a garage and construct a new 
commercial building within the same building footprint. The entire lot is within the 100-year floodplain 
and 200’ Riverfront area. 
Mr. Sarris and Bob Bibbo of Bibbo Brothers were present. [Note: Mr. Bibbo’s assertion that only half 
the lot is in Riverfront Area is incorrect. Per 310 CMR 10.58(2) Riverfront Area under the WPA 
extends 200’ from the Mean Annual High-water Line of the Charles, not 100’, and does not have a 
buffer zone.] Mr. Bibbo described the erosion control plan. The new building will be slightly larger than 
the older one. The garage will not be replaced. He asserted an increase in flood storage capacity. 
The new building will add 10 galleys for storm water, which will overflow to city storm drains; the 
garage area will have 2 new galleys and a catch basin. The existing septic system will be drained 
then filled with sand. The new building will connect to city sewer service. Ms. Abbott reported that 
DEP is satisfied with the revisions made by the applicant since the previous hearing. She had no 
concerns that haven’t already been addressed and recommended the commission issue an Order of 
Conditions, with Waltham’s standard special conditions. Mr. Doyle asked for clarification on a 
previous snow storage comment. Mr. Bibbo confirmed that the owner plans to remove all snow and 
have no storage, and this has been written into the O&M plan. Mr. Dufromont asked for and received 
confirmation that no demolition or construction debris will be stored on site. He asked for and 
received clarifying details on the septic-to-sewer change. Ms. Limonciello asked for clarification on 
the use or storage or large vehicles at this location, due to the proximity to the river. Mr. Bibbo stated 
that a special permit is needed from city council to store heavy trucks here; they will comply with local 
regulations. He noted that the owner has this permission for the adjacent lot [238 Calvary Street]. Ms. 
Shafer asked for confirmation that all DEP comments have been addressed. Ms. Abbott confirmed 
and said the only outstanding point related to the size of the new building’s flood vents, which is not in 
ConCom jurisdiction. Mr. Bibbo will discuss that with the Engineering Department. Mr. Bibbo 
confirmed for Ms. Limonciello that the building will be slab (no basement/excavation). Mr. Donovan 
moved to close the public hearing, seconded by Mr. Fitzgerald. In favor: Doyle, Limonciello, Donovan, 
Shafer, Fitzgerald, Dufromont. Motion passed. Motion to issue an Order of Conditions, including the
Approved 10/22/2026 
standard special conditions. Mr. Donovan seconded. In favor: Doyle, Limonciello, Donovan, Shafer, 
Fitzgerald, Dufromont. Motion passed. 
 
Commission Business 
• Approval of meeting minutes from 9-24-2026. Motion to approve by Mr. Donovan, seconded by 
Mr. Dufromont. In favor: Doyle, Donovan, Fitzgerald, Dufromont. Abstain: Limonciello, Shafer. 
Motin passed. 
 
Correspondence 
• NOTED: National Grid gas main replacement work in the Lakeview neighborhood planned for 
spring/summer 2027. A small portion is in buffer zone to Hardy Pond and presumed exempt 
(maintenance in existing utility footprint). 
• NOTED: MA DEP has reduced drought status in our region to Level 1 –  Mild Drought as of 
September 10. 
• NOTED: DCR correspondence regarding trail bridge damage in Beaver Brook Reservation during 
9/26-27 Nor’easter. Brief discussion. A tree fell on this bridge during the storm. The bridge is on 
the border between Waltham and Belmont, near Rock Meadow. Belmont has also been notified. 
DCR already plans to file an NOI for a larger trail improvement and bridge replacement project 
later this year, which includes this footbridge. Ms. Limonciello recalled a previous bridge project 
in the reservation [316- 0845]. That bridge is in the south section, near the spray park and 
playground. This damaged one is in the northern section and is unrelated. 
• NOTED: Ms. Abbott reported that MWRA notified the commission about damage to the aqueduct 
beneath Waverley Oaks Road (WASM3). Tree root damage was cited. They will be performing 
emergency repairs (exempt work) over the next few days. Brief discussion. The commission is 
familiar with this aqueduct and location because MWRA recently received a permit [316- 0820] 
to replace a section and install a new valve station. That work has not yet begun. 
 
Old Business 
• Conservation Restrictions. Update. Discussion. Mr. Doyle noted that he expected no decision at 
this meeting, but that they should work to understand what the city expects of the commission 
in regard to the certification forms included with the draft CRs. He noted that without confirmed 
holders for the CRs, they can only be considered drafts subject to change. Extensive discussion 
on who a CR holder can be and how that mechanism is intended to work. Mr. Doyle noted both 
that some of these parcels are not in commission jurisdiction, and therefore commission 
involvement carries little weight, and also that even without a CR any work which would be 
regulated under the WPA would still require commission approval. Mr. Daly presented the state 
form included with the draft CR (“Municipal Certification”). He noted that this is recommended 
but not required by the state. He highlighted language which he summarized as asking for the 
commission’s opinion on why it believes this CR is important. Mr. Doyle noted that the 
commission staff has drafted language for this form for each CR. He believes this is good 
language but wants the commissioners to review it. There are 9 total draft CRs, 5 of which have 
jurisdictional areas. One does not seem to have been purchased with CPA funds, but that is not 
a requirement for a CR; a CR can be placed on any parcel. Mr. Doyle suggested that after the 
commissioners review the draft language, they plan to finalize this and return it to the law 
department. He noted that CPC and ConCom have been asking for these CRs for years, so a 
couple of weeks delay seems fine. He noted that these are not yet CRs because no holders 
have been identified; they are more about working toward the goal. Mr. Dufromont noted that in 
the past the CPC had worked with the Waltham Land Trust to create a CR but WLT did not have 
adequate resources. Administering a CR can include significant expense. He noted city land 
purchases along Trapelo Road and the Fernald, with and without CPA funds, which have been
Approved 10/22/2026 
used for general open space but which could theoretically be sold and developed because there 
are no restrictions on them. Mr. Doyle again urged the commissioners to review the draft text. 
He noted that the commission does not have to give a certification,  and could respond to all, 
some, or none of the CRs. Mr. Fitzgerald confirmed that the CPC is also looking at these. He 
stated that he believed there should be specified criteria for certification, to explain, for example, 
why one CR might be certified but another wouldn’t be. Comments that the term “certification” 
on the form and in this situation seems confusing, because that is not really what’s being asked 
for. Mr. Doyle also noted that the ConCom would still have no authority to implement or enforce 
CR terms, outside existing WPA-related duties. He also noted some potential concerns with the 
language of the CRs, specifically citing the “conservation area” reference in the 200 Trapelo 
(Fernald) draft, which is not well defined. He felt that these drafts are progress. Ms. Limonciello 
prompted further explanation of why CR holders are needed and their responsibilities. Ms. 
Shafer proposed asking the law department who would be intended to hold the CRs. The amount 
of protection and durability of CRs was discussed. Mr. Doyle said he sees them as one of 
numerous layers of protection. Ms. Limonciello asked that no decisions be made before the 11/5 
meeting, as she will miss the 10/22 meeting. Mr. Doyle asked if the law department had given 
any deadline for response. Mr. Daly was not aware of one. The commission agreed to keep this 
on the agenda for discussion at the 10/22 meeting in case additional issues arise. 
 
Site Visit Reports 
• 137 Copeland Street. Ms. Abbott has made a tree removal visit and wanted to discuss  with the 
commission to confirm that the tree removal policy is appropriate. An arborist has certified that 
a tree should come down. The policy applies to buffer zone, but this tree is in a jurisdictional 
area. They will top the tree and leave a 20-foot snag in place. Mr. Dufromont commented that if 
the tree is in the wetlands, they should leave the downed portions for wildlife. Ms. Abbott 
confirmed that this is the plan, and that the snag will also benefit wildlife. The commission agreed 
that this removal should be allowed.  While not strictly under tree removal policy language, it is 
still the type of certified hazard tree removal that has traditionally been allowed without a filing. 
 
Committee Reports 
• Paine Estate Forest Management Plan subcommittee. 
o CPC correspondence closing out grant account. Mr. Dufromont reported on the situation. 
CPC has taken the grant back, prompted by a City Auditor policy to reclaim unused funds 
on grants more than 3 years old (the grant was awarded in December 2019). ConCom 
can reapply. Discussion regarding re-applying. Mr. Dufromont and Mr. Donovan still plan 
to meet with Purchasing to get bids in advance and work with them to develop an 
application that will move smoothly through the grant process. 
• CPC: Next meeting scheduled for November 17, 2026. 
 
New Business 
• 590 Lincoln Street. Ms. Abbott noted an RDA for follow -up to 2023 work will be on the next 
agenda. 
Motion to adjourn by Ms. Shafer, seconded by Ms. Limonciello. All present in favor. Motion passed. 
 
Meeting adjourned at 8:21 PM.
